title: Costa Rican Wildlife & Biodiversity
shortDescription: Meet Costa Rica’s astonishing wildlife and ecosystems, from cloud forests to coral reefs.
longDescription: Costa Rica concentrates an outsized share of Earth’s life in a compact territory where two oceans and two continents meet. Misty cloud forests, lowland rainforests, mangroves, wetlands, coral reefs and high páramo create niches for thousands of endemic and migratory species. Conservation, science, and community livelihoods intersect here: more than a quarter of the nation is protected, ecotourism funds ranger programs, and local knowledge guides restoration. This collection presents emblematic species and habitats, emphasizing adaptations, ecological roles, and responsible wildlife watching.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: A slow‑moving arboreal mammal that spends most of its life hanging in the canopy, lowering metabolism to save energy.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Common in Caribbean lowlands and regenerating forests; descends to the ground rarely, often to defecate. Algae and moths live in its fur, forming a miniature ecosystem.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Power lines and road crossings are major hazards. Wildlife corridors, insulated cables, and rescue centers reduce mortality.

sections.heading: Cultural Notes
sections.content: A national icon for patience and calm; campaigns promote respectful, no‑touch encounters.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Nocturnal relative of the three‑toed sloth with a blunter face and two claws on the forelimbs.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Feeds on leaves, flowers, and fruit; excellent climber that prefers dense canopy and sleeping cavities.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Urban expansion fragments habitat. Tree connectivity in towns allows safe movement.

sections.heading: Learning Angle
sections.content: Contrasting two sloth lineages shows convergent slow‑life strategies.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Emerald and crimson bird revered in Mesoamerica. Males grow spectacular tail coverts during breeding.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Cloud forests of Talamanca and Monteverde; disperses seeds of wild avocados, sustaining forest cycles.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Sensitive to warming and deforestation; nest monitoring and reforestation protect populations.

sections.heading: Viewing Ethics
sections.content: Observe at dawn with guides; keep quiet distance to avoid stress.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Brilliant red, yellow, and blue parrot now recovering on the Pacific slope.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Seen in Carara and Osa; pairs bond for life and communicate with far‑carrying calls.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Illegal pet trade and loss of nesting trees were decisive threats; nest boxes and enforcement helped rebound.

sections.heading: Cultural Meaning
sections.content: Flagship of rainforest recovery and community pride.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Critically endangered parrot tied to almendro (Dipteryx panamensis) for nesting and food.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Northern Caribbean lowlands; seasonal movements track fruiting trees.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Corridors, reintroductions, and legal protection of almendro are restoring numbers.

sections.heading: Community Link
sections.content: Festivals celebrate successful chick fledging each season.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Largest cat in the Americas; apex predator whose presence stabilizes food webs.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Ranges in Corcovado and Tortuguero; powerful swimmer that preys on peccaries, turtles, and caimans.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Needs large connected habitats. Camera‑trap networks and livestock‑management reduce conflict.

sections.heading: Cultural Notes
sections.content: Sacred in pre‑Columbian cosmologies and modern conservation stories.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Nocturnal, mid‑sized cat; agile climber with striking rosettes.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Hunts rodents and birds in dense understory across both slopes.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Roadkill and fragmentation threaten gene flow; wildlife underpasses help.

sections.heading: Ecological Role
sections.content: Controls small mammals, limiting crop damage near farms.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: The largest terrestrial mammal in Central America—gentle, shy, and essential seed disperser.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Nocturnal browser of swamps and rainforest; strong swimmer, leaves telltale tracks in mud.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Endangered from hunting and roads; crossing structures and patrols are critical.

sections.heading: Ecological Role
sections.content: Plants large‑seeded trees that shape future forest composition.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Highly intelligent primate known for tool use and complex social dynamics.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Common in Nicoya and Manuel Antonio; opportunistic diet of fruits, insects, and small vertebrates.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Feeding by tourists causes aggression and disease—strict no‑feeding rules apply.

sections.heading: Ethics
sections.content: Store food securely; observe from a respectful distance.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Deep dawn choruses define many forests; sound travels kilometers.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Lives in groups; folivorous diet drives slow, energy‑saving lifestyle.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Electrocution on uninsulated lines is a major cause of death; wildlife bridges save lives.

sections.heading: Community Role
sections.content: Sentinel of forest connectivity in urbanizing regions.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Acrobatic primate with prehensile tail; indicator of intact, mature forest.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Fission‑fusion groups roam large home ranges seeking ripe fruit.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Highly sensitive to hunting and fragmentation; corridors and large reserves are essential.

sections.heading: Learning Angle
sections.content: Highlights the link between frugivores and seed dispersal.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Nocturnal 'honey bear' pollinator with prehensile tail and long tongue.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Visits night‑blooming flowers and fruiting trees; often detected by soft chirps.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Victim of pet trade; education discourages captivity.

sections.heading: Observation
sections.content: Best seen on guided night walks using red lights.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Curious diurnal procyonid with flexible snout used for foraging.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Females form social bands; males are mostly solitary. Adapts to edges and secondary growth.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Human food conditioning leads to conflict; secure trash and no feeding.

sections.heading: Citizen Science
sections.content: Visitor reports help map urban–wildlife interactions.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Day‑active rodent that caches seeds, unintentionally planting forests.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Common near lodges and forest edges; wary, quick sprinters.

sections.heading: Ecology
sections.content: Key partner of hardwood trees that rely on scatter‑hoarding.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Hunting restrictions and habitat mosaics sustain populations.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Nocturnal, spotted rodent with strong hindlegs; prized by predators.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Uses burrows near streams; forages for fallen fruit at night.

sections.heading: Conservation & Threats
sections.content: Overhunting can alter food webs; enforcement and alternatives reduce pressure.

sections.heading: Field Tip
sections.content: Look for tracks and burrow entrances along creek banks.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Iridescent wings flash blue to confuse predators; underside is cryptic brown.

sections.heading: Life Cycle
sections.content: Larvae feed on host plants; adults sip fermenting fruit and sap.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Butterfly farms provide income while easing wild collection.

sections.heading: STEM
sections.content: Great case for structural color and metamorphosis.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Tiny aposematic frog with many color morphs; toxins come from its arthropod diet.

sections.heading: Parental Care
sections.content: Males guard eggs; females deposit unfertilized eggs as tadpole food in bromeliads.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Pet trade and habitat loss are pressures; captive breeding and permits regulate demand.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.content: Model for chemical ecology and behavior.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Translucent belly reveals organs, helping camouflage on leaf undersides.

sections.heading: Habitat
sections.content: Nocturnal along clear mountain streams; eggs laid on leaves above water.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Sensitive to water pollution and chytrid fungus; riparian buffers are vital.

sections.heading: Education
sections.content: Highlights freshwater health and amphibian declines.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: The 'Jesus Christ lizard' can sprint across water using fringed toes and rapid slaps.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Riparian thickets; dives to escape threats and is an agile climber.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Locally common but vulnerable to bank clearing and pets.

sections.heading: STEM
sections.content: Inspires research in biomechanics and robotics.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Large reptile of estuaries and river mouths; notable population at Tárcoles.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Basks on muddy banks; nests on sandy shores; opportunistic predator.

sections.heading: Conservation & Safety
sections.content: Avoid feeding; keep distance from banks; authorized boat tours only.

sections.heading: Management
sections.content: Zoning and education curb human–crocodile conflict.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Smaller cousin of crocodiles with a bony ridge between eyes.

sections.heading: Habitat & Behavior
sections.content: Freshwater wetlands like Caño Negro; ambushes fish and amphibians.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Wetland protection and water quality are key.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.content: Contrasts salt‑tolerant crocodiles with freshwater caimans.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Long‑distance migrant returning to natal beaches; emblematic of Tortuguero.

sections.heading: Life Cycle
sections.content: Females lay clutches at night; juveniles graze seagrass beds, trimming meadows.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Light pollution, plastics, and bycatch threaten survival; patrols and gear changes help.

sections.heading: Responsible Watching
sections.content: Use certified guides, red lights, and keep clear paths for nesting females.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Known for synchronized mass nestings—arribadas—at Ostional.

sections.heading: Ecology
sections.content: Hatchling success depends on beach dynamics and predator cycles.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Community‑managed egg harvest under quotas funds protection and research.

sections.heading: Visitor Tips
sections.content: Follow guide instructions; no flash; maintain distance.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Costa Rica sees both northern and southern populations, extending the season.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content: Breaching and complex songs during breeding off Osa and Marino Ballena.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Vessel speed limits and approach distances reduce disturbance.

sections.heading: Community
sections.content: Whale‑watching sustains coastal livelihoods and marine education.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: The largest fish on Earth—gentle filter feeder occasionally seen near offshore seamounts.

sections.heading: Ecology
sections.content: Follows plankton blooms; often accompanied by remoras.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Global declines from bycatch; marine protected areas and codes of conduct are essential.

sections.heading: Diving Ethics
sections.content: No touching or chasing; keep horizontal distance and avoid flashes.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: Coastal tree with prop roots that stabilize shores and trap sediment.

sections.heading: Ecology
sections.content: Nursery habitat for fish and crustaceans; filters pollutants and stores 'blue carbon'.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Threatened by dredging and development; protected in Térraba‑Sierpe and other estuaries.

sections.heading: Community
sections.content: Sustainable mangrove tours provide income and stewardship.

sections.heading: Information
sections.content: National flower admired for purple blooms; symbolizes beauty and hope.

sections.heading: Ecology
sections.content: Epiphyte that anchors on branches without parasitizing hosts.

sections.heading: Conservation
sections.content: Illegal collection harms wild stocks; cultivation and gardens reduce pressure.

sections.heading: Cultural Notes
sections.content: Gifted during celebrations and featured in school botany projects.
